pairs: Terra autem erat inanis et vacua,
But the earth was empty and unoccupied,
et tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi:
and darknesses were over the face of the abyss;
et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.
and so the Spirit of God was brought over the waters.
Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona:
And God saw the light, that it was good;
and so he divided the light from the darknesses.
And it became evening and morning,
“Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters,
and let it divide waters from waters.”
divisitque aquas, quæ erant sub firmamento,
and he divided the waters that were under the firmament,
ab his, quæ erant super firmamentum.
from those that were above the firmament.
et factum est vespere et mane,
Congregentur aquæ, quæ sub cælo sunt, in locum unum:
“Let the waters that are under heaven be gathered together into one place;
et appareat arida. Et factum est ita.
and let the dry land appear.” And so it became.
And God called the dry land, ‘Earth,’
and he called the gathering of the waters,
Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.
‘Seas.’ And God saw that it was good.
“Let the land spring forth green plants,
et lignum pomiferum faciens fructum juxta genus suum,
and fruit-bearing trees, producing fruit according to their kind,
cujus semen in semetipso sit super terram.
whose seed is within itself, over all the earth.”
And the land brought forth green plants,
et facientem semen juxta genus suum,
both those producing seed, according to their kind,
et habens unumquodque sementem secundum speciem suam.
with each having its own way of sowing, according to its species.
Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.
And God saw that it was good.
Et factum est vespere et mane,
And it became evening and the morning,
Dixit autem Deus: Fiant luminaria in firmamento cæli,
Then God said: “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven.
And let them divide day from night,
et sint in signa et tempora,
and let them become signs, both of the seasons,
and of the days and years.
Let them shine in the firmament of heaven
And God made two great lights:
Et posuit eas in firmamento cæli,
And he set them in the firmament of heaven,
to give light over all the earth,
and to rule over the day as well as the night,
and to divide light from darkness.
Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.
And God saw that it was good.
Et factum est vespere et mane,
And it became evening and morning,
“Let the waters produce animals with a living soul,
et volatile super terram sub firmamento cæli.
and flying creatures above the earth, under the firmament of heaven.”
And God created the great sea creatures,
and everything with a living soul and the ability to move that the waters produced,
quam produxerant aquæ in species suas,
et omne volatile secundum genus suum.
Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.
And God saw that it was good.
and fill the waters of the sea.
And let the birds be multiplied above the land.”
Et factum est vespere et mane,
And it became evening and morning,
Producat terra animam viventem in genere suo,
“Let the land produce living souls in their kind:
et bestias terræ secundum species suas.
and wild beasts of the earth, according to their species.”
Et fecit Deus bestias terræ juxta species suas,
And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their species,
et omne reptile terræ in genere suo.
and every animal on the land, according to its kind.
Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum,
And God saw that it was good.
Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram:
“Let us make Man to our image
And let him rule over the fish of the sea,
and the flying creatures of the air,
and every animal that moves on the earth.”
Et creavit Deus hominem ad imaginem suam:
And God created man to his own image;
to the image of God he created him;
and have dominion over the fish of the sea,
and the flying creatures of the air,
and over every living thing that moves upon the earth.”
Ecce dedi vobis omnem herbam afferentem semen super terram,
“Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant upon the earth,
et universa ligna quæ habent in semetipsis sementem generis sui,
and all the trees that have in themselves the ability to sow their own kind,
and for all the animals of the land,
and for all the flying things of the air,
et universis quæ moventur in terra,
and for everything that moves upon the earth
et in quibus est anima vivens,
and in which there is a living soul,
so that they may have these on which to feed.”
And God saw everything that he had made.
Et factum est vespere et mane,
And it became evening and morning,
